chunks: He said: And informed me Ahmad ibn al-Hasan said: Narrated to me Yahya ibn Ishaq al-Alawi from his father that: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

I asked him about the master of this command after him, he said: The master of the animal. And Abu al-Hasan was in a corner of the house with him, and with him was a Measkan ewe, and he was saying to it: Prostrate to Allah who created you. Then he said: Indeed, he is the one who will fill it with equity and justice, just as it was filled with injustice and oppression.

key_terms.الْبَهْمَة: The animal (specifically a sheep/ewe in this context)
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ: Master of the Command (referring to the Imam)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq identify Imam Musa al-Kadhim as his successor?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* serves as a key evidence for the Imamate of Musa al-Kadhim (a.s), utilizing the descriptive title 'Sahib al-Bahima' (Master of the Beast/Sheep) to identify him amidst the crowd. The Prophet’s instruction to the sheep to prostrate symbolizes the submission of all creation to the Imam’s authority, while the promise to fill the earth with justice echoes the messianic role of the Mahdi, a concept central to Shia eschatology.
